concepts.title: Work Done by a Force
concepts.body: Work is done when a force causes an object to move in the direction of the force. The amount of work depends on the magnitude of the force and the distance the object moves. For example, pushing a box across the floor involves work because the force applied moves the box in the same direction.

concepts.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
concepts.body: Kinetic energy is the energy possessed by an object due to its motion, while potential energy is the energy stored in an object due to its position or state. For instance, a moving car has kinetic energy, and a book placed on a shelf has potential energy due to its height above the ground.

concepts.title: Law of Conservation of Energy
concepts.body: The law of conservation of energy states that energy cannot be created or destroyed; it can only be transformed from one form to another. For example, when a pendulum swings, its potential energy converts to kinetic energy and vice versa, but the total energy remains constant.

formulas.title: Work Done
formulas.body: W = F x s (W in joule J, F in newton N, s in meter m). This formula calculates the work done when a force F moves an object through a displacement s in the direction of the force.

formulas.title: Kinetic Energy and Potential Energy
formulas.body: Kinetic energy = (1/2) m v^2 (m in kg, v in m/s). Potential energy = m g h (m in kg, g in m/s^2, h in m). These formulas calculate the kinetic energy of a moving object and the potential energy of an object due to its height above a reference point.

examples.title: Everyday Example
examples.body: When you lift a bag of groceries from the floor to a table, you do work against gravity. The force applied overcomes the gravitational force, and the bag gains potential energy due to its increased height.

examples.title: Applied Example
examples.body: In a hydroelectric power plant, water stored at a height has potential energy. When it falls, this energy is converted into kinetic energy, which is then used to generate electricity.

mcqs.question: What is the SI unit of work?
mcqs.explanation: The SI unit of work is joule (J). Newton is the unit of force, watt is the unit of power, and pascal is the unit of pressure.

mcqs.question: A car of mass 1000 kg is moving at a speed of 10 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
mcqs.explanation: Using the formula KE = (1/2) m v^2, KE = (1/2) x 1000 kg x (10 m/s)^2 = 50000 J. The other options are incorrect calculations.

mcqs.question: A ball is dropped from a height of 20 meters. Ignoring air resistance, what is its speed just before it hits the ground? (g = 10 m/s^2)
mcqs.explanation: Using the law of conservation of energy, potential energy converts to kinetic energy: mgh = (1/2)mv^2. Solving for v, v = sqrt(2gh) = sqrt(2 x 10 x 20) = 14.14 m/s. The other options are incorrect calculations.
